extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners (KIPO) and patent prosecution professionals interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO guidelines for conducting prior-art searches and substantive examination, including rules for priority claims, citation of prior art, search scope/time coverage, outsourcing searches, and post-search reporting. Intended to guide examiners in assessing novelty, inventive step and procedural formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of law as of filing date (transitional measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Patent Act is revised while an application is pending, transitional measures apply so that provisions of the law shall be applied as of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional/converted applications and applications filed by lawful right holders are accorded the same filing date as the parent (earlier) application; treat such applications according to the law in force as of the parent/earlier filing date. Example: divisional filed July 1, 2009 based on application filed before June 30, 2009 is governed by previous Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority and non-prejudicial-disclosure reference date
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications claiming priority (treaty or domestic) or claiming non-prejudicial disclosures, the provisions of law shall be applied as of the original application's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an application in Korea claiming priority to an original Japanese filing—certain intervening amendments to law (e.g., what counts as prior art) may be applied based on the original filing date; examiner may notify if invention was publicly worked before that filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for prior art is performed during examination to discover the relevant state of the art to assess patentability (novelty and inventive step).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search includes earlier applications under Article 36 and Article 29(3). Examiner may outsource search when necessary (Article 58(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing searches when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary for examination, an examiner may outsource the search for prior art to a specialized organization pursuant to Article 58(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsourced search outcomes must use KIPO-designated format; selection and scheduling handled by Examination Bureau and Patent Examination Support Division. Examiner performs preliminary and confirmation reviews of outsourced results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-search technical analysis (basis of search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before searching, the examiner shall analyze technical subject-matters of the invention; the search should be made on the basis of the claimed invention, but the examiner shall pay due regard to the detailed description/drawings if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on technical subject-matter and claimed features; inspect description/drawings when they provide necessary context or starting points for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of documents cited in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application cites documents in the description, the examiner shall analyze whether they provide starting point of the claimed invention, show current status of technology, explain other solutions, or aid understanding; disregard documents that are not directly related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cited documents are necessary but unobtainable via common methods, request submission from applicant and defer examination until submission. Use cited documents as starting points where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign patent office search results
rubrics_metrics.description: If foreign patent offices or search organizations already conducted a search regarding the claimed invention, the examiner shall review those search outcomes to determine whether they can be used as relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess appropriateness and applicability of such external search reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search scope: databases and document types
rubrics_metrics.description: Search is carried out in systematically accessible collections or databases, primarily patent documents of various countries, supplemented by technical journals, periodicals, books, written materials, microfiche, CD-ROM, DVD-ROM, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all technical fields pertinent to the invention; select sections to consult based on strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search extension to analogous fields judged case-by-case
rubrics_metrics.description: Search strategy should determine sections to consult covering directly relevant technical fields and may be extended to analogous fields if necessary, judged by the examiner in each case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The need to extend depends on outcome of initial searches in directly relevant sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances where search is not required or may be limited
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort is necessary or search may be limited if the claimed invention falls under certain cases where meaningful search is impossible for some/all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated cases: ① amendment beyond scope under Article 47, ② claimed invention not patentable under Article 32, ③ claimed invention incomplete or not industrially applicable under Article 29, ④ lack of unity of invention under Article 45 (claims do not relate to one invention or linked group), ⑤ inability to interpret claims due to lack of clarity/conciseness. In such cases notify applicant and may wait for response; if claims can be understood despite deficiencies, proceed within defined scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time coverage of search (reference dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting a search, examiners should search documents published before the filing date (or, for priority-claim applications, before the priority date); exceptions permit extension to post-filing documents in specific cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: when applying Article 29(3)/(4) or Article 36, or when later documents explain principles or confirm incorrectness of earlier rationale. For priority-claim applications, determine reference date for each claim between earliest prior date and filing date; when ambiguous, decide claim-by-claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of search when lack of novelty/inventive step is clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may suspend search when prior art clearly demonstrates lack of novelty or inventive step for the entire claimed subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend to conserve resources once a clear ground of rejection is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when search disproportionate; use effective method within time/cost
rubrics_metrics.description: If completing the search would take substantial time/energy, examiner shall devise the most effective method to conduct a thorough search within available time and cost; if unable to discover effective prior art despite rational judgment, may suspend the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance thoroughness against resource constraints; document rationale for suspending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent technical features considered in search
rubrics_metrics.description: Search will consider prior art incorporating technical features equivalent to those of the claimed invention, in light of the detailed description; equivalents are not limited to explicitly described features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: claim specifying 'welding' may be interpreted to include other combining means (gluing, riveting) unless explicitly limited to welding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search of dependent claims within independent claim classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for independent claims must include all dependent claims within the identical classification; dependent claims are interpreted as restricted by all features of the claims they depend on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If independent claim subject-matter's patentability is not questioned, no need to further search dependent claims as such. Example provided for pharmacological composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: When claims of different categories exist, include categories as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When application contains claims of different categories (product, process, use), all must be included in the search; however, if a product claim is clearly new/non-obvious, no special effort required to search process or use claims that inevitably result in that product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one claim category present, may consider including other categories desirably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search on description-based subject-matter when no excessive effort required
rubrics_metrics.description: Search shall be made on the basis of the claimed invention, but if no additional excessive efforts are required, the examiner may search for prior art based on invention stated in the description but not in claims, preparing for possible amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to anticipate claim amendments and catch relevant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite prior art only if public availability is clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art used as grounds for rejection shall be cited only if there is no doubt that it was publicly known/worked or described in a publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify publication dates and availability; attach supporting documents where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent-family members and language variants as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a family member was published earlier in a foreign language, a later Korean-language family member may be cited if it establishes that the family document was publicly known before filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may notify the earlier family publication and attach it to rejection notice to demonstrate the earlier public availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of abstracts as prior art (limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner can cite an abstract as prior art for denying novelty/inventive step, but must ground rejection on the contents disclosed in the abstract, not on the full text which is not part of the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventive step assessment requires full text, attempt to obtain full text. If full text unobtainable and abstract used, notify reasons and compare specifically where full texts can be obtained. (Patent court example cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies or URLs of cited documents with notices for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice for rejection must be accompanied by copies of all cited documents, except bulky contents; examiner may copy only pages directly related to the ground for rejection. If applicant has easy Internet access, examiner may state URL and publication number instead of sending copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-patent literature behind paywalls or subject to copying bans, indicate channel to find cited document rather than attaching copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defer citing unpublished 'another application' until publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When examiner discovers prior art that is a not-yet-laid-open application (another application under Article 29(3)), defer examination until that prior art is published; cite it as grounds for rejection only after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not cite unpublished applications as prior art; suspend examination until publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of cited prior art relevance (X/Y/A/O/P/E/T/L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related prior art can be classified depending on relevance: X (single document denying novelty/inventive step), Y (denying inventive step when combined with others), A (related but not X/Y), O (use/exhibition/oral disclosure), P (patent docs before filing date of international application after prior date), E (patent docs disclosed before/after date of international application), T (documents to understand principle/theory or disclosed later), L (documents negating contents or raising priority questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate category when annotating citation sheets and examination reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Report (ER) must indicate relevance and search details
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner completes an Examination Report (ER) before final decision to grant or reject; when identifying cited documents in ER, indicate relevance of each document in citation sheet with X or Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ER may contain keywords and search history used: title of search DB, search formula, number of matches. Examiner may add examination references found during search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include search history and analysis in ER
rubrics_metrics.description: The ER may include keywords and search history used in the prior-art search; search history may list search DB title, search formula, and number of matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent search record to support grounds for rejection or grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and reporting process for outsourced search outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: For externally produced search reports, examiner conducts preliminary review before substantive examination and confirmation review after substantive examination to assess delivery method, appropriateness, accuracy of relevance, balanced composition among documents, and other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner records review outcomes in a Review Statement of Prior Art Search Outcome and reports to Examination Bureau director and Patent Examination Support Division; confirmation review includes analysis report on practical utility of search outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual reexamination obligation for outsourced searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Search service contracts may contain provisions obliging the external organization to reexamine results if examiner evaluates outcomes as unutilized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contractual provisions to ensure quality and allow rework by external search providers when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners to check publication date and content without over-interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall determine whether retrieved prior art provides grounds for rejection regarding novelty, inventive step, enlarged concept of novelty or earlier application; check bibliography to ensure publication date precedes filing date (or priority date); check inventors/applicants for enlarged-concept issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have clear understanding of technical issues disclosed in prior art; avoid acknowledging matters not disclosed in those documents and be cautious not to over-interpret claims without logical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination prior to substantive examination for special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications with priority claim, non-prejudicial disclosure, divisional or converted application, examiner shall conduct formalities examination concerning validity of priority claims or procedures prior to substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to formalities and procedures sections (Part IV Chapter OOO) for details; request amendment or invalidate procedures if physical requirements not met, and provide opportunity for applicant explanation in certain divisional/converted cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim under treaty: eligibility and declaration timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can claim treaty priority is the applicant who filed in a State party or his/her legitimate successor; priority claim must be declared within 12 months from first filing date of the first application on which priority is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants differ between original and subsequent applications, examiner may request evidential documents proving succession; late declaration leads to amendment request and possible invalidation of the priority procedure; procedural amendment scope is limited to correcting self-evident errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim reference date determined claim-by-claim and identity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimed invention in priority claim is identical (including de facto identical) to invention in original application, reference date is filing date of original application; for multiple priority claims, use earliest filing date; where invention is a combination of matter from multiple originals, treat as not stated in original application and use appropriate reference date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects of priority in setting reference date are determined on a claim-by-claim basis; where original application claims priority to an earlier application, the original may not be the 'earliest application' under Paris Convention and retroactive effect may not apply—examiner must state reasons for non-retroactive application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim evidential documents and electronic exchange (DAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents for treaty priority must be submitted within 1 year and 4 months from earliest filing date; failure to submit within prescribed period causes loss of effect. Submission of copies may be exempt when countries participate in on-line exchange (DAS); application number in priority claim may substitute for submission in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may request translations of evidential documents when necessary; failure to submit required translations in Korean may invalidate the priority claim procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim rules and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority claim eligibility is limited to the applicant of the earlier application; domestic priority must be claimed within one year of earlier filing; divisional/converted applications cannot serve as basis for domestic priority; earlier applications invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned cannot serve as basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventions are identical between earlier application and domestic priority claim, reference date is earlier application's filing date; complex domestic priority uses earliest filing date; earlier application is regarded withdrawn after one year and three months; examiner defers further examination until earlier application is considered withdrawn and may defer grant decisions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure claim timing and evidential requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where non-prejudicial disclosure under Article 30(2) is claimed, examiner shall examine whether application was filed within six months from prescribed publication date stated in the application; untimely claim is not overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure claimed to have been made by person with right to obtain patent, examiner checks whether right exists, whether purport is stated in application, and whether evidential document of public disclosure is submitted within 30 days from filing date; for multiple disclosures, claimant must state purport individually with corresponding evidential documents. Pay special attention where discloser differs from applicant or evidential documents are insufficient/incorrect.
